articleTitle: New developments in mixed bipolar/CMOS/DMOS technology for intelligent power applications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Integrated Power Devices
abstract: Describes recent developments in BCD technology, presenting examples of the current state of the art and explaining the trends in smart power IC design. One of the examples is a new standard IC-a dual bridge for motor driving-which is explained at the circuit level; another is an example of the very high complexity smart power ICs that BCD technology makes possible.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimising the design of high power semiconductor packaging for integrated power devices
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Integrated Power Devices
abstract: Discusses the application of power semiconductors where users place many demands on the semiconductor manufacturer. Designing the actual semiconductor itself is one problem. Packaging it in a usable form presents a further new set of conflicting requirements. Introducing intelligence adds yet more to the problems of packaging.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improved fabrication technologies for GaAs power MMICs
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Integrated Power Devices
abstract: Describes the technology enhancements necessary to produce GaAs IC chips that combine small signal and power functions on a single chip. The well established small signal production MMIC process has a final substrate thickness of 200 mu m and the active layers are prepared by ion implantation into semi-insulating GaAs substrates, both these aspects must be retained when fabricating power MMICs in order to maintain a high yield commercially compatible process. The realisation of power MMIC structures under these two main constraints has required the development of a new material doping specification and a novel heatsink structure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A comparison of internal heating and temperature distribution in IGBT and DMOS devices
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Integrated Power Devices
abstract: Local heating effects are simulated for both types of transistor, by solving the current continuity and Poisson equation fully in 2-Dimensions and calculating local heating from the resulting Current Density and Electric Field. The effect of Generation-Recombination heating is also included and compared with the case where this is not significant. Finally this heat-source term is used in the solution of the Heat Equation in order to find the steady state temperature distribution. It is found that strong local heating effects occur in both devices with apparent cooling occurring in some regions where recombination has been ignored, which may have a beneficial effect on the locally heated regions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High-voltage power ICs for motor drives and power supplies
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Integrated Power Devices
abstract: Using new high-voltage integrated circuit (HVIC) technology, a number of integrated circuits have been developed for use in switched-mode power conversion and motor control. These devices have a voltage rating adequate for operation from rectified mains supply. The HVIC technology allows the monolithic integration of power devices, logic circuits and small-signal analog circuits. The analog and digital signal processing is achieved with accuracy and reliability despite the high values of dv/dt and di/dt associated with power switching. Another important feature of these devices is level shifting, whereby signals are conveyed reliably to and from sections of the circuit which are at a high voltage with respect to ground, and which may experience very high values of dv/dt. Furthermore, since the device is required to block high voltage, the field termination and package isolation must meet the necessary standards of integrity and reliability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
